description:
What the OWOX Data Marts TikTok Ads connector loads, and how the pieces fit together. A TikTok advertiser account holds campaigns, campaigns hold ad groups, and ad groups hold ads. The connector loads the settings of each level as current-state tables ([Advertiser Account](./advertiser-account.md), [Campaigns](./campaigns.md), [Ad Groups](./ad-groups.md), [Ads](./ads.md)), the account's saved [Custom Audiences](./custom-audiences.md), and the daily performance of ads as two time-series tables: [Ad Performance](./ad-performance.md) and [Ad Performance by Country](./ad-performance-by-country.md).

Each table repeats the ID of the level above it, so every level joins to its parent on a plain ID: [Ad Groups](./ad-groups.md) to [Campaigns](./campaigns.md) on `campaign_id`, [Ads](./ads.md) to [Ad Groups](./ad-groups.md) on `adgroup_id`, and both performance tables to [Ads](./ads.md) on `ad_id`. Campaigns and Custom Audiences join to the advertiser on `advertiser_id`. The performance tables also carry `campaign_id` and `adgroup_id`, but read them through Ads rather than as a second route to the campaign.

One caution applies to the performance tables: the connector's Data Level setting decides what one row is. The default is the ad level, one row per ad per day. At the advertiser, campaign or ad group level the rows are totals for that level and `ad_id` is not part of the key, so the join to Ads does not apply.
questions: Which campaigns spend the most for the fewest conversions, once spend is divided by conversions?
How do spend and click-through rate change from campaign to ad group to ad for the same objective?
Which countries do ads spend in, and which of them convert?

Advertiser Account.description:
One row per advertiser account listed in the connector's Advertiser IDs: the advertiser ID, its name, company name and account currency. The connector reads it from the authorized ad accounts endpoint, whose documentation lists only the advertiser ID and name for each account, so `company_name` and `currency` are in the schema but are not documented for that endpoint.

Every other table carries `advertiser_id`; this is the table to label them with the account name.
questions: Which advertiser accounts does this connector load, and what are their names?
Which advertiser accounts belong to the same company?
In which currency is each advertiser account set up?

Campaigns.description:
One row per campaign: its name, objective and objective type, campaign type, operation and secondary status, budget and budget mode, bid type, and create and modify times. It holds settings, not results; spend and clicks are in Ad Performance, which reaches a campaign through Ads and Ad Groups.

The connector's Include Deleted setting is off by default; when it is on, campaigns in every status are requested. Join it to Advertiser Account on `advertiser_id` for the account name.
questions: How many campaigns does each objective type have, and how many are currently enabled?
Which campaigns have a daily budget and which have a total budget?
Which campaigns were modified in the last 30 days?

Ad Groups.description:
One row per ad group: its name, the campaign it sits in (`campaign_id` and `campaign_name`), status, budget and budget mode, bid type and bid price, optimization goal and event, placements, and targeting such as gender, age groups, languages, locations and audience IDs. Several of these are lists stored as JSON.

An ad group is the level that ads sit in, so this table is the bridge between a campaign and its ads. The targeted audience IDs in `audience_ids` are a list inside one column, so they do not join row by row to Custom Audiences.
questions: How many ad groups does each campaign have, and how many are paused?
Which optimization goals and bid types does each campaign use?
Which ad groups have a schedule that has already ended?

Ads.description:
One row per ad: its name and status, the campaign and ad group it belongs to (`campaign_id`, `adgroup_id` and their names), and the creative: creative type, ad format, ad text, call to action, video and image IDs, landing page URL, deep link and tracking URLs. It holds settings, not results; daily numbers are in Ad Performance, which joins here on `ad_id`.

The connector's Include Deleted setting is off by default, so deleted ads are not loaded unless it is turned on. Join it to Ad Groups on `adgroup_id` for the ad group's bids and targeting.
questions: How many ads of each creative type does each ad group run?
Which landing pages are used by the most ads?
Which ads have a call to action set, and which do not?

Ad Performance.description:
Daily ad performance: impressions, clicks, spend, click-through rate, reach, frequency, conversions with cost per conversion and conversion rate, video play and completion-point views (2s, 6s, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%), and profile visits, likes, comments, shares and follows. With the default Data Level, one row per ad per `stat_time_day`, keyed by `ad_id`, `stat_time_day` and `advertiser_id`.

The connector asks the API for a fixed list of metrics, so schema columns such as `cost`, `engagement`, `video_views`, `video_completion`, the `real_time_` columns, `result` and `cost_per_result` are in the table but are not requested; use `spend` for the amount spent. The unit of the amounts is not stated in the table; read it from the advertiser account. Join it to Ads on `ad_id` for the ad's name and creative.
questions: What did each ad spend and return per day over the last 30 days?
Which ads have the highest cost per conversion, and how many conversions do they have?
Which ads keep the most viewers to the end of the video, relative to video plays?

Ad Performance by Country.description:
Daily ad performance split by country: the same impressions, clicks, spend, conversion and video metrics as Ad Performance, with `country_code` (a two-letter ISO country code) added to the key. With the default Data Level, one row per ad, country and `stat_time_day`.

The connector asks for the same fixed list of metrics as Ad Performance, so `cost`, `engagement`, `video_views` and the `real_time_` columns are not requested; use `spend`. There is no table of countries here, so `country_code` is read as it stands. Join it to Ads on `ad_id` for the ad's name and creative.
questions: Which countries bring the most conversions, and at what cost per conversion?
How does click-through rate differ by country for the same ad?
Which ads spend in more than one country?

Custom Audiences.description:
One row per custom audience of an advertiser: its ID and name, audience type, coverage (`cover_num`, the number of matched users on TikTok), when it was created, whether it is valid and expiring, and when it expires. An audience becomes invalid after it expires.

The audiences endpoint takes the advertiser ID as a request parameter, and the connector stamps it on each row as `advertiser_id`. Ad groups list the audiences they target in `audience_ids`, an array column, so there is no row-by-row join to this table.
questions: Which custom audiences have expired or are about to expire?
Which audience types cover the most users?
How many valid audiences does each advertiser account have?
